title: Self-Supervised Pretraining for PHM: What Transfers, What Does Not, and What Federating It Costs
abstract: arXiv:2610.35280v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Self-supervised pretraining has produced capable time-series foundation models, but its value for Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) has not been measured under leakage-controlled conditions. We measure it on a corpus of 47 public PHM datasets, harmonized to a single tensor contract and partitioned so that 11 datasets are withheld from pretraining in full. Transfer turns out to be task-dependent: a compact channel-independent Transformer encoder (801,808 parameters) pretrained with masked patch prediction raises fault-classification macro-F1 from 0.350 to 0.812 on CWRU and from 0.569 to 0.951 on HSG18, yet on CMAPSS remaining-useful-life estimation no pretrained checkpoint reliably improves upon a from-scratch baseline. We pretrain under two regimes---centralized, and simulated cross-silo federated with ten clients grouped by physical domain---holding architecture, objective, source data and optimization budget fixed. translated_title: 面向故障预测与健康管理（PHM）的自监督预训练：什么能迁移、什么不能迁移，以及联邦化预训练的代价
translated_abstract: 自监督预训练已经催生出强大的时间序列基础模型，但其在故障预测与健康管理（PHM）领域的价值尚未在防泄漏控制的严格条件下得到测量。我们在包含47个公开PHM数据集的语料库上对此进行评估，这些数据集被统一到单一的张量规范并加以划分，其中11个数据集完全未参与预训练。结果表明迁移效果依赖于具体任务：一个紧凑的通道独立Transformer编码器（801,808个参数）经掩码补丁预测预训练后，将CWRU数据集上故障分类的宏F1从0.350提升至0.812，将HSG18数据集上的宏F1从0.569提升至0.951；然而在CMAPSS剩余使用寿命（RUL）估计任务上，没有任何预训练检查点能够稳定地超越从零训练的基线。我们在两种模式下进行预训练——集中式，以及模拟跨机构孤岛的联邦式（十个客户端按物理领域分组）——同时保持架构、训练目标、源数据和优化预算不变。另外两个发……
tldr: 该研究在47个公开PHM数据集上系统评估了自监督预训练的迁移价值，发现预训练能大幅提升故障分类性能（CWRU宏F1从0.350升至0.812）但对剩余使用寿命估计无稳定改进，并进一步对比了集中式与联邦式预训练的差异。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically measures the transfer value of self-supervised pretraining on 47 public PHM datasets, finding that pretraining dramatically improves fault classification (CWRU macro-F1 rising from 0.350 to 0.812) but offers no reliable gains for remaining-useful-life estimation, and further compares centralized versus federated pretraining regimes.
